figure1.title: Guaranteed funding and marginal obligation.
figure1.note: Uniform hypothetical report noise; sigma/e* denotes an assumed standard deviation. B=EUR 7.925m, p=EUR 25/tCO2e. At zero noise and F=B, the selected constant contract has m=0; the upper endpoint is open.

figure2.title: Upfront financing and required marginal obligation.
figure2.note: Uniform hypothetical noise with the same benchmark budget and cap. Financing gaps are assumed bankable and payable from the floor before verification. At zero noise, g=B is excluded for any positive target.

figure3.title: Distribution-dependent marginal obligations.
figure3.note: Hypothetical uniform and Gaussian errors have equal variance at each sigma/e*; each schedule is calibrated to the same expected budget. Gaussian reporting is a signed-error sensitivity, with a negative-report tail.

figure4.title: A mean-preserving spread can raise the marginal obligation.
figure4.note: Dimensionless counterexample, not event data. Adding an independent symmetric unit noise raises variance from 1 to 2 and the local expected slope from 0.50 to 0.75; expected payment remains 0.80 and p=1.
